files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
Scans and Gaussian splats open in the viewer: laser, drone and phone scans as points, and the photo-real captures phone apps make as they were captured, each thinned to what the device can draw. A link can now reopen a model exactly as you see it, or open one of its notes. Files that record no unit can be given one, saved for everyone. And once an admin lists the sites allowed, a public link's model can be shown on another website.

### Added
- Links to a view: "Copy link to this view" in the tools panel (or the L key) copies a link that reopens the model as you see it, with the same camera, shading, lighting, cross-section and exploded view. Each annotation has "Copy link to this note", which opens the Annotations panel on that note, and each bookmark has "Copy link". The link points at the file, so only people who can open it see it. On a public link, and in the viewer opened from Files, a link sets the camera, and those viewers have a "Copy link to this view" button of their own; if you manage a public link of a file, "Copy public link to this view" copies that link with the camera. The tools panel's "Copy View Link", which carried the camera only, is now this, and its links still open.
- Units for files that don't record one: STL, OBJ, PLY, OFF and 3DS files, and FBX files without a unit, can be marked as drawn in millimetres, centimetres, metres, inches, feet or US survey feet, under "File units" in the model statistics or the Print check card. The unit is saved with the file for everyone who can open it, on public links too; only people who can edit the file can change it. Sizes, measurements, Print check and Send to Slicer follow it, and the file itself is left as it is. Files that record their unit, such as 3MF, glTF or STEP, show it.
- Show a model on another website: once an admin lists the sites allowed to embed, under Administration settings › 3D Viewer › Embedding, "Copy embed code" in the tools panel copies a frame to paste into such a site, for a public link to the file without a password. It shows the model, from the current angle if you like, with full screen, a download when the link allows it, and a link to open it in Nextcloud. If the link later gets a password, expires or is deleted, the frame says the model is no longer shared. Embedding is off until a site is listed, and every other Nextcloud page still refuses to be shown in a frame.
- Point clouds: laser, drone and phone scans in LAS, LAZ, E57, PCD and XYZ, and PLY files with no faces, open as points. A Scan section in the tools panel colours them by the file's colours, height, intensity or classification, sets the point size, and says which way is up, which is saved with the file for everyone like the unit. Scans up to 2 GB open; past what the device can draw (20 million points on a desktop, fewer on tablets and phones) they are thinned evenly, with a note saying how much is shown, and survey coordinates keep their millimetres. Measurement snaps to points and the cross-section cuts them. Print check, shading, comparison and export are off for scans, each with a note saying why. LAS and LAZ files take their unit from their coordinate system; E57 is metres. A chemistry `.xyz` says it lists atoms.
- Gaussian splats: the photo-real captures phone apps make, in `.splat`, `.spz` and splat `.ply` files, open as they were captured. You can orbit them, bookmark and link views, take snapshots and record turntable videos, and they get thumbnails and work on public links and in embeds. A Splat section in the tools panel says which way is up, saved with the file for everyone like a scan's. Splats up to 1 GB open on a desktop (512 MB on a tablet, 256 MB on a phone); past what the device can draw (8 million splats on a desktop, fewer on tablets and phones) they are thinned evenly, keeping the colour that changes with the view, with a note saying how much is shown. Measurement, annotations, the cross-section, Print check, transform, exploded view, shading, comparison, export and VR are off for splats, each with a note saying why: a splat has no real surface.

### Fixed
- Cancel loading pressed while the viewer was still getting ready, before the model's download had started, did nothing: the model loaded anyway. It now stops that load, and Retry still loads the model.
- Cancel loading pressed while the viewer was still getting ready, after the model had been read, also let the model appear. It now stops it there too.
- Cancelling the load of a file picked from the file browser showed an "Aborted" error. Cancelling is no longer reported as an error.
- A file picked from the file browser that failed to open showed its error twice. It now shows it once.
- Send to Slicer sent a model's numbers as they are, which a slicer reads as millimetres: a glTF, in metres, arrived a thousand times too small, and an FBX in centimetres ten times too small. The copy it sends is now written in millimetres.
- The Print check card was hard to read: its text, the Y up/Z up switch, the warnings and the Check wall thickness button took the page's colours while the card took the colours of the panels drawn over the model, which are the reverse of the page's, so on Nextcloud's dark theme they came out light grey and pale red on a light card. The card now uses the same colours as the statistics, measurement and annotation panels throughout, and the legend's swatches match the colours on the model.
